answer: Latency-terrace admission gating: each identity must sustain a minimum inter-arrival gap between its first N transactions, measured against a rolling baseline; bursts above the gap hit a rate ceiling. At the network's zenith of load, the gate widens, so attackers who spin up identities in parallel collide with tighter spacing checks. The mirror effect: honest agents pacing naturally pass, while mass-registered identities must serialize their traffic to fit. An attacker pays real wall-clock delay per identity plus idle capacity held across the terrace of waiting periods.
